title: Tile size guide for Indian rooms
excerpt: Which tile size suits which room, what 2x2 and 2x4 actually mean, and where large formats pay off — and where they don't.

children.text: Indian tile shops use a shorthand that confuses everyone the first time. "2x2" means 2 feet by 2 feet — 600x600 mm. "2x4" is 600x1200 mm. Once you can translate, choosing a size becomes a design and budget question instead of a vocabulary test.
What each size does best

children.text: Practical rules we give customers every day
Bigger tiles = fewer joints = an airier room, but the subfloor must be flat or you will see lippage under raking light.
In bathrooms, smaller floor tiles (or textured 600x600) handle slopes toward the drain better than one giant slab.
Marble-look prints read better across a full tile, so large formats suit dramatic veining; small formats suit plain tones.
Diagonal or herringbone layouts increase cutting wastage — plan 12–15% instead of the usual 8–10%.
Bring your room measurements to the showroom (or use our tile calculator) and we will show the same design in two or three sizes so the difference is obvious.

title: Vitrified vs ceramic vs natural stone
excerpt: The honest differences that matter in an Indian home: water absorption, maintenance, feel underfoot and lifetime cost.

children.text: Customers ask this daily, and the honest answer is: none of the three is universally better — they fail differently. Here is the comparison we draw on the counter.

head: Vitrified / porcelain tile
Ceramic tile
Natural marble
Granite
rows: Soft — will scratch and polish out

children.text: How we frame the decision
Rental or budget build: vitrified 600x600 is the pragmatic answer.
Forever home, willing to maintain: marble is a living material many families love for decades.
Kitchens and stairs: granite or full-body vitrified; both shrug off decades of traffic.
Want the marble look without the upkeep: printed marble-look vitrified at a fraction of the price.

title: How many boxes do I need? Quantity and wastage, explained
excerpt: A no-nonsense method to estimate tile boxes, why wastage is 8–12% for most rooms and more for diagonal layouts, plus our calculator.

children.text: Under-order and you risk a shade mismatch from a different batch; over-order and you waste money. The method below is what our counter staff actually use.
The method
Measure each floor/wall as length × width; add the areas of every surface together.
Add wastage: 8–10% for straight layouts in regular rooms, 12–15% for diagonal, herringbone, many doorways, or very small rooms.
Divide by the box coverage (printed on every product page here) and round UP to whole boxes.
Keep one spare box per home after laying — future repairs will not match a new batch.
Example: a 15 ft × 12 ft living room is 180 sq ft. At 10% wastage you need 198 sq ft. The Bianco Carrara 600x1200 covers 15.5 sq ft per box, so 198 / 15.5 = 12.8 → 13 boxes.

body.text: Odd-shaped rooms, patterns and site conditions change the numbers. Treat the calculator as a planning estimate and confirm the final order with your installer or with us.
